title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: Major's consequence invalid — not everything later done about the non-elect flows from absolute reprobation; Vasquez: some effects are of common providence
pass_a_gloss: We answer that the consequence of the Major is invalid; and in this we affirm the adversaries are deceived, that the decree of absolute reprobation being posited they assume as a consequence that from this decree flows whatever afterward is done about these non-elect or reprobate. But on the contrary Vasquez rightly observed, That neither in the predestined nor in the reprobate is every effect of the providence of God an effect of predestination or of reprobation, but that some is an effect of common providence, In 1. quaest. 23. artic. 4. cap. 4. disp. 93.
pass_b_english: We answer that the Major's consequence is invalid. The adversaries err in this: having posited absolute reprobation, they take it as following that whatever is later done about these non-elect or reprobate flows from that decree. Vasquez rightly notes the contrary: neither in the predestined nor in the reprobate is every effect of God's providence an effect of predestination or reprobation — some is an effect of common providence (In 1 q.23 a.4 c.4 disp. 93).
source_text: Consequentiam Majoris invalidam esse respondemus; atque in hoc falli adversarios affirmamus, quod posito absolutae reprobationis decreto quasi consequens assumunt, ex hoc decreto manare quicquid postea circa hosce non-electos sive reprobatos peragitur. At e contra recte observavit Vasques, Nec in praedestinato nec in reprobato omnem effectum providentiae Dei esse praedestinationis aut reprobationis, sed aliquem esse effectum communis providentiae, In 1. quaest. 23. artic. 4. cap. 4. disp. 93.
